# The Line Between Us

By nine on Saturday, the village square had six bare posts and one paper notice that said WELCOME in letters too small to read from the road. Leni, who had volunteered to decorate it, wanted bunting stretched high across the arch. “People should see it before they turn the corner.” Mrs Bell was setting out folding tables for the festival. New neighbour Jo had moved into the green cottage two days ago, and Leni wanted the welcome to feel like a real welcome, not a notice pinned to a door.

The bunting lay in a basket, but its string had run out. Leni found Mrs Bell coiling a red-and-white spool by the village hall. “Could I borrow it? I’ll bring it back after we hang everything.” Mrs Bell passed it over. “The spool, please. The string you use can stay where it’s useful.” Leni promised, and carefully put the spool in her canvas bag. It was heavier than she expected; she liked that it felt like a proper job.

Jo was sitting on the square bench with one ankle in a walking boot and a cane leaning against the seat. Leni had seen them arrive with two boxes and a plant. “You’re the new neighbour,” she said, then immediately wished she had found a better opening. Jo laughed. “That’s what the boxes say.” Leni explained the festival and the bare posts. Jo listened, then asked, “Is there something I can do, or am I just here to be welcomed?”

“We can hang the bunting on the arch,” Leni said. “I could climb the low side and pass the string over.” Jo’s smile disappeared. “Please don’t. My ankle can’t climb, and I don’t want your festival to start with a fall.” Leni looked up at the arch. It seemed a long way up now. “I thought I was making it grand.” “Grand is fine,” Jo said. “Being able to help is better.” Leni heard the difference between doing the job for Jo and doing it with Jo.

They examined the square instead of the arch. Two waist-high posts stood near the path; Jo could reach them from the bench, and Leni tested each one with a careful tug. One post wobbled. The other pair, by the low garden wall, held firm. Jo picked up two paper triangles. “Blue and gold,” they said. “My old harbor town used those colors on its lanterns.” Leni let Jo arrange the pieces. The pattern looked brighter than the red-and-white basket, and Jo’s hands were already part of the decoration.

Leni made a loop in the borrowed string and pulled. It slid loose. “This spool is no good,” she muttered. Jo turned the string between their fingers. “It’s smooth, not bad. Try a second loop.” They practiced on a short tail, using a little of the string, then leaned back together. The knot held against the basket handle. “A knot you trust is better than a ladder,” Jo said. Leni tucked the practice piece away instead of pretending it had never failed.

Clouds hurried over the rooftops. A gust lifted the paper triangles, and a cold drop struck Leni’s cheek. The low posts would be wet soon; the square was exposed, and the unsteady pair would not hold a line. The tall arch was still there, but it would need climbing and the wind could tug at anyone up high. “We could wait,” Leni said. Jo looked toward the village hall and its deep porch. “Or we can welcome people under a roof now.” Leni considered the posters already sent around the village. Moving the display meant giving up her grand arch, but not the festival.

They carried the basket and spool to the hall rail, where the roof kept the boards dry. The rail was low enough for Jo to reach without standing, and Leni measured a shorter span than the outdoor line would have needed. “Room for six triangles,” she said. “Seven,” Jo answered, sliding the blue and gold one to the middle. Leni tied each end. Jo made the final double loop, then tugged until it held. Nobody climbed; nobody had to watch from the side. The string had turned a bare rail into a welcome.

Mrs Bell opened the hall doors as the first neighbours arrived. Leni stood by the bunting. “We had a bigger plan,” she said, “but this is the one we could make together.” Jo pointed to the blue-and-gold triangles. “They’re from my old town. This one is my favourite.” An older couple stopped to ask about the colors. Jo told them about the harbor lanterns, and they stayed to help arrange cups. Leni noticed that people were gathering around Jo, not merely being directed toward them.

The rain pattered on the porch while the festival filled the hall. Children followed the low line to the tables; a little girl reached up to straighten a triangle, and Jo showed her how to tie the corner securely. When the music started, Leni danced with Mrs Bell between the chairs while Jo kept time with a spoon against a mug. The arch outside remained bare. Leni saw it through the window and was surprised to find she did not mind. The welcome was happening here, at the height where Jo could join it.

When the last cups were collected, Leni carried Mrs Bell’s spool back to the hall cupboard. The remaining string was wound neatly around it; the used length still held the bunting in place. “You put it to work,” Mrs Bell said. Jo had already promised to show the neighbors the harbor pattern another day, and now there were three people asking to learn the knot. Leni was glad she had returned the spool with something useful left on it, not just an apology for borrowing it.

On the way home, Jo walked slowly beside Leni, cane tapping the dry edge of the path. “I thought moving here would mean starting every story from the beginning,” Jo said. Leni pointed back at the lit hall. “We’ve started one.” Behind them, the low bunting stirred gently whenever the door opened. It had not reached the highest place in the square, but it had made room for a new neighbor to hold one end—and for everyone else to come closer.

'''Short scene prose rendered from the actions and state that actually occurred.'''


def render(scene_id, params, before, after):
    if scene_id == 'borrow_spool':
        return ('Leni found Mrs Bell winding a red-and-white spool beside the village hall. '
                '“Could I borrow it for the welcome bunting? I’ll bring back the leftover string.” '
                'Mrs Bell passed it over. “The spool, please—not the bunting.” Leni looked toward '
                'the bare square posts. They seemed to be waiting for a party.')

    if scene_id == 'meet_neighbor':
        return ('Jo, the new neighbor, sat on the square bench with a walking boot beside them. '
                '“I wanted to help with the festival,” Jo said, “but I’m not climbing anything '
                'until this ankle heals.” Leni started to offer to do it alone, then stopped. '
                '“Would you help me choose where it goes?” Jo smiled. “Now that’s a proper invitation.”')

    if scene_id == 'color_vignette':
        return ('Jo held two paper triangles beside the basket. “Blue and gold. The harbor lanterns '
                'in my old town used those colors.” Leni passed over the yellow pieces. Jo arranged '
                'them without leaving the bench, and Leni carried the choice into their plan. The '
                'bunting would bring a small piece of Jo’s old home into this one.')

    if scene_id == 'knot_vignette':
        if before['knot.slips']:
            return ('“This string slides when it’s wet,” Jo said, rubbing the test knot. Leni almost '
                    'blamed the spool, but Jo showed her a second loop and a firm pull. They practiced '
                    'on a short tail, used ten centimetres, and tested it against the basket handle. '
                    'It held. “A knot you trust is better than a ladder.”')
        return ('Jo suggested testing a knot before trusting it with the bunting. Leni looped the '
                'string twice around a basket handle, and they both leaned back. It held. They used '
                'ten centimetres for the practice, then Jo showed Leni how to keep the loop flat. '
                '“Now we know,” Jo said. Leni liked having checked together.')

    if scene_id == 'choose_layout':
        if after['layout.mode'] == 'square':
            return ('Leni and Jo looked from the arch to the low posts. The square was calm and dry; '
                    'both posts held firm, the spool reached far enough, and Jo could reach the line. '
                    '“No climbing,” Jo said. “We can both reach this.” Leni chose a line fifty-five '
                    'centimetres high. The arch stayed bare, but the square had a plan for both of them.')
        if before['weather.rainy']:
            reason = 'Rain was already stippling the open square'
        elif before['weather.gusty']:
            reason = 'Gusts were tugging at the loose paper triangles'
        elif not before['anchors.sturdy']:
            reason = 'One of the low posts shifted under Leni’s careful test'
        elif before['Jo.reach_cm'] < 55:
            reason = 'Jo could not comfortably reach the square line'
        elif before['spool.remaining_cm'] < 180:
            reason = 'The borrowed string was too short for the exposed square span'
        else:
            reason = 'The unpracticed knot would not stay secure on the exposed line'
        return (f'{reason}. Leni looked up at the arch, then toward the village hall porch. '
                '“We could wait,” she said. Jo pointed to the low rail under the roof. “Or welcome '
                'people now, where I can help.” They carried the basket inside and chose a line '
                'thirty-five centimetres high. The grand arch could stay bare.')

    if scene_id == 'hang_bunting':
        place = 'the square posts' if after['layout.mode'] == 'square' else 'the hall rail'
        height = after['layout.height_cm']
        colors = 'blue and gold' if after['bunting.pattern'] == 'blue-and-gold' else 'red and white'
        knot_line = (' Jo used a double loop on the rail.' if after['knot.reinforced'] and not after['knot.practiced']
                     else ' The knot held when they tested it.' if after['knot.practiced']
                     else ' Their knot held on the first careful tug.')
        return (f'Leni clipped the {colors} triangles along {place}, keeping the line at {height} '
                f'centimetres. Jo tied the final knot from the bench, without climbing or stretching '
                f'for the arch.{knot_line} The borrowed string now had a job: holding the welcome '
                'where both neighbors could reach it.')

    if scene_id == 'welcome':
        location = 'the square' if after['festival.place'] == 'square' else 'the village hall'
        pattern = 'blue-and-gold' if after['bunting.pattern'] == 'blue-and-gold' else 'red-and-white'
        return (f'Mrs Bell opened the doors at {location}, and the first neighbors followed the '
                f'{pattern} bunting to the tables. “We had a grander plan,” Leni said, “but this is '
                'the one we made together.” Jo pointed out a favorite triangle and told its story. '
                'People gathered to listen; the welcome had become something Jo could give, too.')

    if scene_id == 'return_spool':
        return ('After the first rush of the festival, Leni carried Mrs Bell’s spool back to the '
                'hall cupboard, with the unused string wound neatly around it. The used length still '
                'held the bunting in place. “You put it to work,” Mrs Bell said. Jo was showing a '
                'neighbor the knot. Leni was glad to return the spool with something useful left on it.')

    if scene_id == 'ending_square':
        return ('The square filled beneath the low line, and nobody needed a ladder or a rescue. '
                'Jo showed two children how to tie the same secure knot, while Leni welcomed the '
                'late arrivals. The arch remained empty; the square did not. By the time the music '
                'started, Jo was laughing with people who had come to meet their new neighbor.')

    if scene_id == 'ending_hall':
        return ('Rain tapped on the porch while the village hall filled beneath the low bunting. '
                'Jo welcomed the neighbors from the bench and taught a child the double loop. Leni '
                'watched the bare arch through the window and found she did not mind. The festival '
                'had opened on time, the string was doing its job, and Jo belonged in the middle of it.')

    raise ValueError(f'No prose for scene: {scene_id}')

from copy import deepcopy
from dataclasses import asdict
from itertools import product
import unittest

from storyscenes.mini_adventures.local_play import LocalPlay
from storyscenes.runtime import StoryError
from .world import Parameters, SCENES, generate, guard, initial, play_scene, replay, validate


class VillageFestivalTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def check_row(self, row):
        params = Parameters(**row['parameters'])
        episodes = replay(params, row['path'])
        expected = []
        for episode in episodes:
            data = asdict(episode)
            data['events'] = list(episode.events)
            expected.append(data)
        self.assertEqual(expected, row['episodes'])
        self.assertEqual(len(row['path']), row['scene_count'])
        self.assertEqual(len(row['path']), len(set(row['path'])))
        self.assertEqual(row['story'], '\n\n'.join(e.text for e in episodes))
        self.assertEqual(row['final_state'], episodes[-1].after)
        self.assertTrue(row['final_state']['story.ended'])
        self.assertTrue(row['final_state']['story.outcome'])
        state = initial(params)
        for episode in episodes:
            self.assertEqual(episode.before, state)
            self.assertTrue(guard(episode.id, state))
            self.assertTrue(episode.events)
            for event in episode.events:
                self.assertTrue(event['changes'])
                for key, value in event['requires'].items():
                    self.assertIn(key, state)
                    self.assertEqual(state[key], value)
                for key, change in event['changes'].items():
                    self.assertEqual(state[key], change['before'])
                    self.assertNotEqual(change['before'], change['after'])
                    state[key] = change['after']
                validate(state)
            self.assertEqual(state, episode.after)
            self.assertGreaterEqual(len(episode.text.split()), 40)
            self.assertLessEqual(len(episode.text.split()), 70)

    def test_two_lengths_over_one_hundred_seeds_and_exact_replay(self):
        for seed, count in product(range(100), (7, 8)):
            with self.subTest(seed=seed, count=count):
                row = generate(seed, count=count)
                self.check_row(row)
                self.assertEqual(row, generate(seed, count=count))
                optional = {'color_vignette', 'knot_vignette'} & set(row['path'])
                self.assertEqual(len(optional), count - 7)
                self.assertEqual(row['path'][-1], 'ending_square' if row['final_state']['layout.mode'] == 'square'
                                 else 'ending_hall')

    def test_explicit_parameter_recipes_reach_both_endings(self):
        square = Parameters(spool_length_cm=240, gusty=False, rainy=False,
                            posts_sturdy=True, jo_reach_cm=70, knot_slips=False)
        hall = Parameters(spool_length_cm=180, gusty=False, rainy=True,
                          posts_sturdy=True, jo_reach_cm=70, knot_slips=False)
        self.assertEqual(generate(17, count=7, params=square)['final_state']['story.outcome'], 'shared_square')
        self.assertEqual(generate(17, count=7, params=hall)['final_state']['story.outcome'], 'sheltered_hall')

    def test_every_parameter_is_validated_and_consequential(self):
        invalid = (
            {'spool_length_cm': True}, {'spool_length_cm': 99}, {'spool_length_cm': 321},
            {'jo_reach_cm': False}, {'jo_reach_cm': 44}, {'gusty': 1},
            {'rainy': 'false'}, {'posts_sturdy': 0}, {'knot_slips': None},
        )
        for values in invalid:
            with self.subTest(values=values), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                Parameters(**values)
        safe = Parameters(spool_length_cm=240, gusty=False, rainy=False,
                          posts_sturdy=True, jo_reach_cm=70, knot_slips=False)
        slippery = Parameters(spool_length_cm=240, gusty=False, rainy=False,
                              posts_sturdy=True, jo_reach_cm=70, knot_slips=True)
        self.assertEqual(generate(5, count=7, params=safe)['final_state']['story.outcome'], 'shared_square')
        self.assertEqual(generate(5, count=7, params=slippery)['final_state']['story.outcome'], 'sheltered_hall')
        short = Parameters(spool_length_cm=120, gusty=False, rainy=False,
                           posts_sturdy=True, jo_reach_cm=70, knot_slips=False)
        low_reach = Parameters(spool_length_cm=240, gusty=False, rainy=False,
                               posts_sturdy=True, jo_reach_cm=50, knot_slips=False)
        weak = Parameters(spool_length_cm=240, gusty=False, rainy=False,
                          posts_sturdy=False, jo_reach_cm=70, knot_slips=False)
        windy = Parameters(spool_length_cm=240, gusty=True, rainy=False,
                           posts_sturdy=True, jo_reach_cm=70, knot_slips=False)
        for params in (short, low_reach, weak, windy):
            self.assertEqual(generate(5, count=7, params=params)['final_state']['story.outcome'], 'sheltered_hall')

    def test_optional_vignettes_are_enacted_and_omittable(self):
        params = Parameters()
        base = generate(4, count=7, params=params)
        self.assertFalse({'color_vignette', 'knot_vignette'} & set(base['path']))
        after_meeting = replay(params, ('borrow_spool', 'meet_neighbor'))[-1].after
        colors = play_scene(params, after_meeting, 'color_vignette')
        self.assertEqual(colors.after['bunting.pattern'], 'blue-and-gold')
        self.assertTrue(colors.after['Jo.chose_colors'])
        practiced = play_scene(params, after_meeting, 'knot_vignette')
        self.assertTrue(practiced.after['knot.practiced'])
        self.assertEqual(practiced.after['spool.remaining_cm'], after_meeting['spool.remaining_cm'] - 10)
        with_color = replay(params, ('borrow_spool', 'meet_neighbor', 'color_vignette'))[-1].after
        without_color = after_meeting
        self.assertNotEqual(with_color['bunting.pattern'], without_color['bunting.pattern'])

    def test_borrowed_object_and_locations_remain_consistent(self):
        params = Parameters(spool_length_cm=240)
        row = generate(8, count=8, params=params)
        state = initial(params)
        for episode in row['episodes']:
            self.assertEqual(episode['before'], state)
            for event in episode['events']:
                for key, change in event['changes'].items():
                    state[key] = change['after']
                validate(state)
            self.assertEqual(state, episode['after'])
            if state['layout.mode'] == 'hall':
                self.assertEqual(state['festival.place'], 'hall')
                if not state['bunting.hung']:
                    self.assertEqual(state['bunting.location'], 'basket:hall')
        final = row['final_state']
        self.assertEqual(final['spool.owner'], 'Mrs Bell')
        self.assertEqual(final['spool.holder'], 'Mrs Bell')
        self.assertEqual(final['spool.location'], 'bell_shed')
        self.assertTrue(final['spool.returned'])
        self.assertEqual(final['spool.remaining_cm'] + final['spool.used_cm'], final['spool.length_cm'])
        self.assertEqual(final['bunting.location'], 'square_line' if final['layout.mode'] == 'square' else 'hall_rail')
        self.assertGreater(final['string.display_cm'], 0)

    def test_illegal_scene_and_failed_local_action_do_not_mutate_caller(self):
        params = Parameters()
        state = initial(params)
        original = deepcopy(state)
        with self.assertRaises(StoryError):
            play_scene(params, state, 'choose_layout')
        self.assertEqual(state, original)
        play = LocalPlay(state, actors=('Leni',), validate=validate)
        saved_state, saved_events = deepcopy(play.state), deepcopy(play.events)
        with self.assertRaises(StoryError):
            play.act('illegal_unknown_change', **{'not.a.state.key': True})
        self.assertEqual(play.state, saved_state)
        self.assertEqual(play.events, saved_events)

    def test_scene_guards_and_endings_follow_the_selected_middle(self):
        square = Parameters(spool_length_cm=240, gusty=False, rainy=False,

        state = replay(square, ('borrow_spool', 'meet_neighbor', 'choose_layout',

        self.assertTrue(guard('ending_square', state))

        finished = play_scene(square, state, 'ending_square').after
        self.assertFalse(guard('borrow_spool', finished))
        with self.assertRaises(StoryError):

# The Line Between Us

A standard-library-only, offline mini-adventure set at a village welcome festival. Leni borrows Mrs Bell’s spool of string and works with new neighbor Jo to hang bunting at a safe, reachable height. The executable pack is new; the `kite` directory name is only the isolated harness path.

## Run and replay

From the repository root:

```bash
python -m storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world --seed 0 --scenes 8
python -m storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world --seed 41 --scenes 7
python -m unittest storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.test_world
```

The command prints the selected prose. `generate(seed, count=7 or 8, params=...)` returns a JSON-native trace; `replay(params, path)` reproduces each scene’s state, event trace, and text. The local play actions use the shared `LocalPlay` helper. Scene search is seeded, bounded, and speculative branches are never included in the returned path or trace.

## Explicit ending recipes

These recipes work for either supported length. Optional scenes can be present in an eight-scene route, but do not change the selected ending in these examples.

```python
from storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world import Parameters, generate

# Calm, dry, sturdy square posts; enough string; Jo can reach; knot holds.
square = Parameters(spool_length_cm=240, gusty=False, rainy=False,
                    posts_sturdy=True, jo_reach_cm=70, knot_slips=False)
row = generate(0, count=7, params=square)
assert row['final_state']['story.outcome'] == 'shared_square'

# Rain makes the exposed square unsuitable, so the completed welcome is sheltered.
hall = Parameters(spool_length_cm=180, gusty=False, rainy=True,
                  posts_sturdy=True, jo_reach_cm=70, knot_slips=False)
row = generate(0, count=8, params=hall)
assert row['final_state']['story.outcome'] == 'sheltered_hall'
```

A slippery knot, short spool, gusts, rain, unstable posts, or insufficient reach also selects the hall. When the hall is used, its low rail provides a safe alternative; an insecure knot is reinforced with a rail hitch in an enacted local action. `knot_vignette` can instead practice a double loop before the layout decision. It consumes ten centimetres and can make the square line feasible when other conditions allow it. `color_vignette` is an optional, persistent design choice from Jo. Seven-scene stories omit both optional vignettes; eight-scene stories include exactly one.

## State and outcomes

The six validated parameters are spool length, gusts, rain, post stability, Jo’s reach, and whether the string slips. They change the physical actions available and/or the ending. Leni and Jo remain at the selected festival location; the basket moves with them; the hung bunting stays on its actual line; the spool remains Mrs Bell’s property; and used plus remaining string is conserved. Both endings require an opened festival and the returned spool. `shared_square` finishes at the safe outdoor low line. `sheltered_hall` finishes a complete welcome under cover rather than leaving it as a future plan.

Every scene has a state-changing local action. Omitted scenes do not execute effects. `LocalPlay` validates each candidate before committing it, so a failed local action does not mutate the caller or its existing trace.

## Limits

This is a small scenario model, not general physics: wind, knot reliability, reach, post stability, and string length are simplified into explicit constraints. The setting has two display locations and two endings; the children do not split up, scenes cannot repeat, and crowd behavior is only represented where it changes the welcome. Prose is authored per scene and conditioned on enacted outcomes, not generated by an LLM. Mechanical tests cannot establish literary quality.
